subject: Blackstone on-prem deployment: node fabric, storage hardening & onboarding checklist
messages:
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.ai>
To: Adam Cole <adam.cole@blackstone-corp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-11-20 09:12 -0800
Subject: Blackstone on-prem discovery — node fabric and storage pre-work

Adam — thanks for taking the time earlier. Per our call, I want to capture a concise preflight so we can scope an on-site/install window and a minimal BOM. Please confirm the bullets below and add any constraints we missed: 

- Air-gap / limited outbound: you mentioned management network will have tightly restricted egress; confirm whether outbound to redwood control plane (control-plane telemetry/heartbeats) is permitted or if we need full air-gapped install.
- Rack footprint: 6U reserved for the cluster; expected to contain master/control nodes + object-store appliance. Final node counts TBD.
- Storage preference: you listed either Ceph/RBD or vendor-provided NFS appliance for persistent block storage. Which is the preferred default?
- NVMe for KV cache: do you want local NVMe on every inference node (for KV cache) or centralized NVMe pool with volume backed across nodes?
- Backup / nightly replication: required retention and whether an on-prem tape/archive is used.
- Compliance: SOC2 evidence required, plus KMS integration for envelope encryption.

If you can respond with short answers, we’ll propose a node-pool layout (control/infra/gpu/cpu/storage) and a hardened network plan (management VLAN, data VLAN, BGP uplinks, ACLs). I’ll loop in Marissa and Karthik for the design and Laura for the operational handoff.

Thanks,
Nikhil Sharma
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
nikhil@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0134
From: Adam Cole <adam.cole@blackstone-corp.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@blackstone-corp.com>, Ellen Park <ellen.park@blackstone-corp.com>
Date: 2025-11-20 11:03 -05:00
Subject: Re: Blackstone on-prem discovery — node fabric and storage pre-work

Nikhil — thanks. Quick answers below and I attached the high-level requirements doc + network diagram. 

- Egress: Management VLAN will allow outbound to specific IPs only. We cannot permit continuous outbound telemetry to a SaaS control plane. We expect an air-gapped deployment with a customer-managed control plane or a proxy-to-proxy arrangement.
- Rack: Confirmed 6U (we can expand if required).
- Storage: Preference is a vendor NFS appliance for long-term persistent volumes; however, we accept Ceph RBD for performance-sensitive volumes. Want recommendation for which PV classes should be on NFS vs RBD.
- NVMe: Prefer local NVMe on GPU nodes for KV cache (low-latency). Centralized NVMe is acceptable for non-latency-critical workloads.
- Backup/replication: 30-day online retention, 1-year archival to our air-gapped archive (S3-compatible appliance that only accepts pushes from on-prem). Nightly rsync or snapshot export is okay.
- Compliance: SOC2 is required; KMS integrates with our HSM (PKCS#11). TLS everywhere and disk encryption at rest is mandatory.

One more thing: procurement wants clarity on SLA tiers (S1/S2) and an install SLA for on-site support (two-day install window max once hardware arrives).

Adam
Director, Infrastructure Operations
Blackstone Capital Partners
adam.cole@blackstone-corp.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Adam Cole <adam.cole@blackstone-corp.com>
Cc: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-11-21 07:45 -08:00
Subject: Proposed node-pool and storage mapping for Blackstone on-prem

Adam — appreciate the fast reply and the attachment. Based on your constraints, here’s our recommended mapping (high level):

1) Control plane (3 nodes, management VLAN)
   - Specs: 2x 32vCPU, 256GB RAM, 1x 1.6TB NVMe (OS + etcd)
   - Isolated on dedicated management/top-of-rack switch; no external NAT aside from a proxy allowed IP list.

2) Infra / system services (2 nodes)
   - Specs: 16vCPU, 128GB RAM, redundant uplinks, small NVMe for local caches (logging, fluentd buffer)

3) Compute-GPU (3–6 nodes initial)
   - GPU: prefer A40/A100 depending on availability (we’ll provide a quantity-based throughput estimate)
   - Local NVMe: NVMe on each GPU node for KV cache (recommended: 1TB NVMe per node)
   - Kubernetes taints for inference workloads; separate quota for batch vs real-time.

4) Compute-CPU (2 nodes)
   - Lighter workloads, model proxies, batch preprocessors

5) Storage / Block target (2 nodes + vendor NFS appliance)
   - For long-lived PVs: mount vendor NFS (SLA-backed appliance) as the default slow PV class.
   - For high-performance PVs (model weights, persistent caches): use Ceph RBD deployed across the two storage nodes (3rd-party recommend 3 nodes for production Ceph; we can run an RBD cluster on top of the NFS if you prefer).

Data paths and durability: NVMe for ephemeral and KV cache; RBD for high-iops durable volumes; NFS for large dataset mounts and slow storage. Nightly snapshots of RBD exported to the appliance via rbd export or rsync to S3-compatible gateway.

Security/hardening notes:
- KMS/HSM: integrate using PKCS#11 for disk keys; we’ll provide a sidecar that does envelope encryption for object export.
- No direct outbound: we’ll ship an offline control-plane bundle and a small proxy image that you can run in a DMZ to push minimal health telemetry (optionally disabled).
- Network policy: eBPF CNI recommended (finer L7 controls).

Questions for you:
- Will procurement sign off on 3-node Ceph (recommended) or prefer to keep Ceph out entirely and lean on the vendor NFS appliance?
- Are you able to allocate a separate L3 management subnet for control-plane-only traffic?

If that looks aligned, Karthik and I will draft an install-runbook and an inventory sheet for procurement.

—Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Adam Cole <adam.cole@blackstone-corp.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-11-22 10:08 -05:00
Subject: Network design checklist and deployment constraints

Adam / team — adding the network constraints and operational checklist we’ll need to finalize before scheduling an install. Small, actionable items below: 

- BGP / Uplink: Do you prefer BGP peering for cross-rack routing or static routes? We recommend BGP for scale and resiliency.
- MTU: Confirm 9000 for jumbo frames on data VLANs (required for NVMe-oF and Ceph).
- ACLs: Provide explicit ACL table for the management proxy IPs (we’ll provide a minimal allowlist).
- Time sync: NTP vs PTP — NTP OK but PTP recommended if you run time-sensitive tracing.
- DNS: Internal DNS entries for control-plane endpoints (we’ll provide SRV records).
- Firewall: We need to open ports 6443 (k8s API), 2379-2380 (etcd), 6783/6784 (flannel/weave if used), custom ports for Ceph and NFS -- we’ll generate a port matrix.
- Monitoring: We will deploy a local metrics stack; if you want remote scraping, that will require limited egress to our monitoring collector.

Operational considerations:
- Install SLA: Redwood provides 2-day onsite install support if hardware arrives by 09:00 local the prior day (we’ll staff a 2-person team). Additional days billed per SOW.
- Cutover window: recommend a 4-hour maintenance window for cluster bootstrap and join operations; we’ll test images on a staging rack before production.

I’ll attach a draft port matrix and MTU checklist to the runbook. Once we have your answers on BGP/MTU/ceph vs nfs, we can lock the BOM and schedule a preliminary dry-run.

—Karthik
Platform Architect, Redwood Inference
From: Adam Cole <adam.cole@blackstone-corp.com>

Date: 2025-11-24 09:34 -05:00
Subject: Re: Blackstone on-prem discovery — node fabric and storage pre-work

Thanks all — this is getting us close. Answers below: 
- BGP: we can do BGP peering.
- MTU: agree to 9000 for data VLANs.
- Ceph vs NFS: Procurement prefers vendor NFS appliance as the default for long-term PVs; however we will allow a small 3-node Ceph ring for high-performance PVs (weights, model caches) if you recommend it. 3-node Ceph acceptable.
- Management subnet: we will allocate a dedicated /26 for control plane traffic.
- SLA: Procurement will accept the 2-day install SLA with a 4-hour bootstrap window. We’ll attach the term sheet and procurement contacts (see attachment).

Next steps: please produce a final install-runbook + BOM and a short SOW amendment with the Ceph 3-node option as a line item (we’ll decide which option to sign after you show cost delta). Also include an estimate for remote support hours and emergency on-call fees.

Adam
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.ai>
To: Adam Cole <adam.cole@blackstone-corp.com>, Procurement <procurement@blackstone-corp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-11-24 16:07 -08:00
Subject: Re: Blackstone on-prem discovery — node fabric and storage pre-work

Adam / procurement team — great, thanks for the clarity. We’ll produce the following by COB Monday: 

- Install runbook (step-by-step bootstrap, control-plane ledger, port matrix, MTU checklist)
- BOM with two options: (A) vendor NFS appliance + no Ceph; (B) vendor NFS + optional 3-node Ceph for high-perf PVs (cost delta included)
- SOW amendment with install SLA, 2-day on-site support, remote support rates, emergency on-call rates
- Draft encryption/KMS integration steps for your HSM (PKCS#11 flow)

I’ll share a draft Drive link and DocuSign stub for the SOW when ready. If you want to accelerate, Marissa can run an architecture dry-run in our lab next week and provide throughput numbers for the different node types.

Action items assigned:
- Marissa: lab throughput & NVMe sizing (ETA: Tue)
- Karthik: port matrix + BGP config template (ETA: Tue)
- Laura: procurement-ready BOM and SOW template (ETA: Mon COB)

Thanks — looking forward to the next step.

Nikhil
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
